statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58649 is an information disclosure issue in the .NET SDK's dotnet watch: its browser refresh server does not adequately validate the origin of cross-origin WebSocket connections, which can expose IL and PDB information. Microsoft lists .NET SDK 10.0.100 through 10.0.110 as affected and 10.0.111 as fixed for the 10.0.1xx feature band (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/441, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58649). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Its dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap package holds the matching .NET SDK, 10.0.1NN for build 10.0.NN-r0. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: dotnet-watch.dll is in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, one copy per package at that SDK's version, and no other package holds it: 10.0.102 to 10.0.110 in the first nine builds and 10.0.113 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with a fixed SDK.
